# Dimension 4 — Pricing, plans and quota

One of the two stated drivers for the move. Source details in
[citations](../citations.md).

**Every figure below is quoted from a page fetched 2026-08-21. No figure comes
from model knowledge.** Where a vendor does not publish a number, this file says
so rather than estimating.

## Subscription prices

### ChatGPT [16]

| Plan | Price as written |
|---|---|
| Free | `$0 /month` |
| Go | `$8 /month` |
| Plus | `$20 /month` |
| Pro | `From $100 /month` |
| API Key | no price — "Pay only for the tokens Codex uses, based on API pricing" |
| Business | `$20 / user / month*` — "*2+ users, billed annually. $25 per user per month when billed monthly." |
| Enterprise & Edu | not stated — "Contact sales" |

Pro's two tiers are pinned only indirectly, by the same page's Voice section and
a Pro bullet: "Pro 5x ($100/month)" and "Pro 20x ($200/month): Unlimited voice
access" [16]. The Pro card itself says only "From $100 /month" and "Choose 5x or
20x higher rate limits than Plus."

The main `chatgpt.com/pricing` page's price elements did not render on fetch —
the cards show a bare "/ month" [32]. All ChatGPT prices here come from [16].

### Claude [59]

| Plan | Price as written |
|---|---|
| Free | `$0` |
| Pro | `$17 — Per month with annual subscription discount ($200 billed up front). $20 if billed monthly.` |
| Max | `From $100 — Per month` |
| Team Standard | `$20 — Per seat / month if billed annually. $25 if billed monthly.` |
| Team Premium | `$100 — Per seat / month if billed annually. $125 if billed monthly.` |

**The Max 20x price is not stated on this page.** The Max card gives one figure,

## Quota — the two vendors are not comparable, and that is the finding

### OpenAI publishes numeric ranges

Codex allowances, **Local Messages per 5-hour window** [16]:

| Model | Plus / Business | Pro 5x | Pro 20x |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-5.6 Sol | 10–100 | 50–500 | 200–2,000 |
| GPT-5.6 Terra | 25–200 | 125–1,000 | 500–4,000 |
| GPT-5.6 Luna | 250–2,000 | 1,250–10,000 | 5,000–40,000 |
| GPT-5.5 | 15–80 | 75–400 | 300–1,600 |
| GPT-5.4 | 20–100 | 100–500 | 400–2,000 |
| GPT-5.4 mini | 60–350 | 300–1,750 | 1,200–7,000 |

Note the ranges are 10× wide. These are estimates, not entitlements — a related
help page says OpenAI "publishes estimated usage ranges, not a fixed message
count".

Window structure [16][34]:

> "The usage limits for local messages and cloud chats share a five-hour window.
> Additional weekly limits may apply." [16]

> "Using a full banked reset resets both your 5-hour and weekly usage windows.
> As a result, your weekly reset date will move to roughly seven days after you
> redeem it." [34]

**The weekly limit is never quantified.** "May apply" is the entire statement.
The five-hour Codex window is also **not described as rolling** anywhere in the
fetched pages — the same page calls the *Voice* allowance "rolling five-hour
windows" but does not extend that word to Codex [16].

Two further carve-outs: Enterprise/Edu on flexible pricing "have no fixed rate
limits - usage scales with credits"; and `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` "is governed by a
separate usage limit that may adjust based on demand" [16].

**Data-quality note:** the same allowance table's cloud-chats and code-reviews
columns render "Not available" for every plan, contradicting the page's own
feature table. Treated as an extraction artifact; no cloud-chat or code-review
allowance is reported here [16].

### Anthropic publishes multipliers only

> "Every plan has usage limits that reset on a rolling five-hour session window,
> and paid plans add weekly limits on top. Your activity across Claude on web,
> desktop, mobile, and Claude Code all draws from the same pool… **so there's no
> fixed message count.** Free covers everyday questions. Pro gives you at least
> 5x more usage per 5-hour session than Free. Max gives you 5x or 20x more usage
> per 5-hour session than Pro." [59]

> "Claude Code is included in all paid plans. It shares the same usage limits as
> the rest of your plan, so your work in the terminal and your chats draw from
> one pool." [59]

Anthropic's dedicated "Use Claude Code with your Pro or Max plan" support
article states **no window size, no reset cadence, no weekly cap, no message
count** [60]. That absence is notable given it is the article a Claude Code
subscriber would read first.

The most recent limits change found is dated **2026-05-06**: "we're doubling
Claude Code's five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based
Enterprise plans" and "removing the peak hours limit reduction on Claude Code
for Pro and Max accounts" [61]. That article is 3.5 months old as of this
research and nothing fetched confirms it is still the latest word. Its API
rate-limit table did not survive the fetch (almost certainly an image), so no
numbers are recoverable from it [61].

A third Claude Code limit exists beyond session and weekly: a **model-specific
Opus limit** [56]. Its size is not published. Critically:

> "These windows are shared across all models, so switching models with `/model`
> doesn't restore access" [56]

— though it does keep you working after the Opus-specific message.

### Consequence

**No like-for-like quota ratio between Codex and Claude Code can be computed
from published sources.** OpenAI publishes wide message-count ranges per model
per plan; Anthropic publishes relative multipliers with an explicit "no fixed
message count". Any numeric Codex-vs-Claude quota comparison would be
fabrication.

## Credits — a mechanism you cannot price

OpenAI's credit rate card, **credits per 1M tokens (input / cached input /
output)** [16][33]:

| Model | Input | Cached input | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-5.6 Sol | 125 | 12.50 | 750 |
| GPT-5.6 Terra | 50 | 5 | 300 |
| GPT-5.6 Luna | 5 | 0.5 | 30 |
| GPT-5.5 | 125 | 12.50 | 750 |
| GPT-5.4 | 62.50 | 6.250 | 375 |
| GPT-5.4 mini | 18.75 | 1.875 | 113 |
| GPT-5.3-Codex | 43.75 | 4.375 | 350 |

Formula [33]:

> "Total credits = (input tokens / 1,000,000 × input rate) + (cached input
> tokens / 1,000,000 × cached input rate) + (output tokens / 1,000,000 × output
> rate)"

Consumption: "A typical Codex task using GPT-5.6 Sol may consume between 5 and
40 credits per task" [33]; "GPT-5.6 usage averages 5-40 credits per message"
[16]. "Codex does not charge for cache writes" [33].

**The blocking gap: no fetched page states a dollar price per credit.** The
dedicated credits help article [35] covers expiry ("Credits are valid for 12
months from purchase"), non-refundability, non-transferability, auto-top-up and
the possibility of a negative balance — and never gives a rate. Neither does the
rate card [33], the Codex pricing page [16], or the plan article [34].

Confirmed only that purchase is possible: "Eligible Plus and Pro users can buy
credits without changing plans" [34]; "Enterprise and Business can purchase
credits for more access" [32].

**Consequence:** the entire Codex credit rate card and the "5–40 credits per
message" average **cannot be converted to money** from cited sources. The
overage path is un-priceable.

Scope caveat: the rate card article is titled for Business and Enterprise/Edu
and explicitly routes individuals elsewhere ("For Plus or Pro credit rates, see
Using Credits for Flexible Usage in ChatGPT") [33], so its credit rates are not
established as applying to a Plus or Pro individual.

## API pricing — where a real comparison is possible

Per 1M tokens, USD.

### OpenAI, standard tier [30]

| Model | Input (short / long) | Cached input | Cache writes | Output (short / long) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | $5.00 / $10.00 | $0.50 / $1.00 | $6.25 / $12.50 | $30.00 / $45.00 |
| `gpt-5.6-terra` | $2.00 / $4.00 | $0.20 / $0.40 | $2.50 / $5.00 | $12.00 / $18.00 |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | $0.20 / $0.40 | $0.02 / $0.04 | $0.25 / $0.50 | $1.20 / $1.80 |
| `gpt-5.3-codex` | $1.75 | $0.175 | — | $14.00 |

Batch and Flex are both listed at half the standard short-context rates; Fast
mode at double [30]. Regional data-residency endpoints carry "a 10% uplift for
models released on or after March 5, 2026" [30].

### Anthropic [58]

| Model | Base input | 5m cache write | 1h cache write | Cache hit | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Fable 5 | $10 | $12.50 | $20 | $1 | $50 |
| Claude Opus 5 | $5 | $6.25 | $10 | $0.50 | $25 |
| Claude Sonnet 5 | $2 | $2.50 | $4 | $0.20 | $10 |
| Claude Haiku 4.5 | $1 | $1.25 | $2 | $0.10 | $5 |

Batch is a flat 50% discount on both directions [58]. Dated statement:

> "The $2/$10 per million input/output token pricing for Claude Sonnet 5,
> announced at launch as introductory pricing through August 31, 2026, is now
> the standard price. The previously scheduled increase to $3/$15 per million
> input/output tokens on September 1, 2026 will not occur." [58]

### Two adjustments any honest comparison must make

**1. The tokenizer is not the same.**

> "Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer…
> This tokenizer produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text. The
> exact increase depends on the content and workload shape. Claude Sonnet 4.6
> and earlier models use the previous tokenizer." [58]

Anthropic states this against its own older models, not against OpenAI. **The
size of the distortion between the two vendors' tokenizers is not quantified by
any fetched source.** Headline per-token prices are therefore not directly
comparable, and this research does not attempt a corrected comparison.

**2. Long context is priced differently.** Anthropic: "Claude 4.6 and later
models… include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing. (A
900k-token request is billed at the same per-token rate as a 9k-token request.)"
[58]. OpenAI charges a separate long-context column at roughly double the
short-context rate [30]. For long agentic sessions this is a structural
difference in cost shape, not a rounding detail.

## Fast mode — different bargains

| | Speed gain | Cost multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| Codex | "increases supported model speed by 1.5x" [17] | GPT-5.6 and GPT-5.5 at **2.5x** credits; GPT-5.4 at **2x** [17] |
| Claude | "up to 2.5x faster speeds… for Opus 5" [59] | **2x** standard pricing [59] |

Codex fast mode is a ChatGPT-credit feature: "With an API key, Codex uses API
token pricing instead, and ChatGPT credit multipliers don't apply. API Priority
processing has its own billing rate; for GPT-5.6, it costs 2x the Standard API
token rate" [17]. Controls: `/fast on|off|status`, or persist with
`service_tier = "fast"` plus `[features].fast_mode = true` [17].

Anthropic's fast mode is Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 only, at $10/MTok input and
$50/MTok output, unavailable on Opus 4.7 and not available with the Batch API
[58].

## The only real-world cost figure either vendor publishes

**Anthropic** [56]:

> "Across enterprise deployments, the average cost is around **$13 per developer
> per active day** and **$150-250 per developer per month**, with costs
> remaining **below $30 per active day for 90% of users**."

Scope, which matters: this is API-token-billed enterprise deployment cost, not
subscription cost, and "per month" is per active usage.

**OpenAI** [33]:

> "On average, Codex costs approximately **$100–$200 per developer per month**,
> though actual costs vary significantly depending on the model used, the number
> of concurrent instances, automations, and fast mode."

These two ranges overlap almost exactly ($150–250 vs $100–200). Neither is
methodologically described — no sample size, no workload definition, no time
window. Treat them as vendor-stated ballparks, not measurements.

Two Claude Code figures that materially change burn rate and have no Codex
counterpart in the fetched set [56]:

- **Cache lifetime:** "an hour on a subscription" but "drops to five minutes
  once you're drawing on usage credits"; `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` restores
  the hour. A cache miss "reprocesses your full context".
- **Agent teams:** "approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when
  teammates run in plan mode, because each teammate maintains its own context
  window and runs as a separate Claude instance."

The second is directly relevant if a heavy Claude Code user's quota pressure
comes from parallel agents rather than long sessions — because Codex's Ultra
reasoning mode also spawns subagents [7], the same multiplier plausibly applies
there, but no source states it.

## A migration hazard worth flagging

> "If you have an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable set on your system,
> Claude Code will use this API key for authentication instead of your Claude
> subscription… resulting in API usage charges rather than using your
> subscription's included usage." [60]

The symmetric Codex hazard is the reverse of the same coin: signing in with an
API key means "Codex uses standard API pricing instead of included ChatGPT plan
credits" and loses Codex cloud entirely [4].

## Gaps and limitations

1. **No dollar-per-credit rate** for OpenAI credits, from any source [16][33]
   [34][35]. The overage path cannot be priced.
2. **No Max 20x price** from any source [59].
3. **No numeric Claude Code allowance** — Anthropic publishes multipliers and
   explicitly states there is "no fixed message count" [59].
4. **No numeric Codex weekly limit** — "Additional weekly limits may apply" is
   the whole statement [16].
5. Whether the Codex five-hour window is rolling or fixed is not stated [16].
6. The 2026-05-06 Anthropic doubling [61] may have been superseded; nothing
   fetched confirms current state, and its rate-limit table was an image that
   did not survive the fetch.
7. A `"50% of weekly limits*"` cell on `claude.com/pricing` — the only numeric
   weekly-limit figure anywhere in the Anthropic sources — could not be anchored
   to a row or column after extraction, and its footnote is absent. Not reported
   [59].
8. The two vendors' "typical cost" figures [33][56] carry no methodology and
   should not be treated as measurements.
9. Cross-vendor per-token comparison is confounded by an unquantified tokenizer
   difference [58].
